This miscellaneous appeal having been heard and reserv
 orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, Justice Achal K
 Paliwal pronounced the following:
 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 05.03.2022 passed by 28th MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.1600039/2016 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Arunkumar Chhatterjee, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,64,773/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 Medical expenses -Rs.55,773/-

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal should have assessed the compensation on the basis of multiplier method.
The income of the deceased should be assessed at least Rs.15,000/- per month.
The deceased was an advocate in profession, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in thecase.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.4,50,000/- (i.e. Rs.15000x12-1/2 personal expenses x 5 (multiplier))

Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
Loss of filial consortium -Rs.1,76,000/-
 Medical expenses -Rs.55,773/-
 ------------------

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Joy Chatterjee vs Drs Dilip Road Lines Pvt. Ltd. on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97754614/

7. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.4,50,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
